spec.title: Project activity and agent operations workspace

status.comment: Owner priority of 2026-09-15: first project switching, global/project activity and a navigable subagent network with real output. This reorders delivery without removing chat, questions, planning or managed-terminal scope.

p.primary-experience: The initial Quicklens workspace centers on selecting a project, viewing activity across all authorized projects or the selected project, inspecting the actual network of coordinators and subagents, and selecting an agent to see its available output and current work. These operations are the first product acceptance scenario. Chat, rich questions, plan views and optional terminal control are integrated into this workspace rather than made prerequisites for its usefulness.

p.shared-canvas: A future unified canvas is distinct from the initial portfolio card page. It provides one pan/zoom coordinate space containing project regions and their task/milestone/agent projections. Scene references retain project/context/object identity, and explicit known cross-project relations may cross region boundaries. Selecting an object resolves its own project-scoped card or agent output. A shared camera or saved board layout is presentation state and does not merge agent contexts, plans or execution authority. Existing shared data contracts support this projection; a card grid is not claimed to implement the canvas.

p.activity-scopes: Activity has explicit all-authorized-projects, project/context and selected-actor scopes, with filters for events requiring attention and retained history. Global activity preserves project labels and stable paged ingestion ordering with source provenance; it does not imply a shared plan or causal clock. A private/project view means scoped visibility, not a separately duplicated journal. Viewing or marking an event read does not acknowledge an agent's inbox delivery or answer a pending question.

p.agent-network: The agent view represents coordinators, native subagents and managed workers with stable actor/session/attempt identities. Parent, delegation, communication or waiting relationships are shown only when sourced from the actual host or shared server. Agent names are labels, not routing identity. The agent network is distinct from the semantic task/goal graph, with explicit links between an execution actor and its assigned work where known. Selecting an agent preserves project scope and exposes its public output, lifecycle and available controls.

p.output-inspection: Output inspection shows captured public messages, tool/progress output and result references for the selected actor. Native actors expose only observed supported output and explicitly state unavailable or incomplete coverage; their display is not a fabricated terminal. Managed actors additionally expose their real terminal under PROP-006 control capabilities. Reading outputs or switching actors does not start a new model turn, reread the project boot or interrupt running work.

p.product-purpose: Lens makes Codex and other agent products useful as a coherent multi-project development system with VibeVM context, observable delegation and shared user interaction. The shared server supplies project/execution visibility and continuity while the configured agent products perform their actual work. Product-neutral contracts preserve this purpose when the selected agent changes. No claim about a competitor, future acquisition or provider policy is a technical requirement.
